# `tfctl run start`

The `tfctl run start` command starts a new run on a workspace.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start WORKSPACE [options]
```

## Description

The `tfctl run start` command creates a new plan and apply run with the most recent configuration. 

<Note>

If auto-apply is enabled on the workspace and no errors occur, the plan is automatically applied.

</Note>

Use `--plan-only` to create a speculative plan-only run that is never applied. This overrides the workspace's auto-apply setting.

## Arguments

- `WORKSPACE`: (Required) Workspace ID or workspace name.

## Flags

- `--organization=NAME`: Organization name. Required when using a workspace name instead of ID.
    - Optional.
    - Data type: string
    - Default value: Auto-resolved from profile or Terraform cloud config

- `--debugging-mode`: Enables trace logging for this run. Sets `TF_LOG=trace` in the Terraform environment for this run.
    - Optional.
    - Data type: boolean
    - Default value: `false`

- `--message=TEXT`: A message to attach to the run.
    - Optional.
    - Data type: string
    - Default value: None

- `--allow-empty-apply`: Allow the run to proceed even if the plan has no changes. Useful for applying a side effect such as a Terraform upgrade when no other changes are present.
    - Optional.
    - Data type: boolean
    - Default value: `false`

- `--plan-only`: Create a speculative plan-only run that is never applied. Overrides the workspace's auto-apply setting.
    - Optional.
    - Data type: boolean
    - Default value: `false`

### Global flags

Refer to [Global flags reference](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/global-flags) for information about flags you can use with all commands.

## Examples

The following examples demonstrate how to start a new run on a workspace.

### Start a new run in a workspace by ID

The following example starts a new run in a workspace using its workspace ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start ws-abc123
```

### Start a new run in a workspace by name

The following example starts a new run in a workspace using its name and organization.

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start my-workspace --organization my-org
```

### Start a plan-only run that is not applied

The following example starts a plan-only run that is not applied automatically.

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start ws-abc123 --plan-only
```

### Start a run with a custom message

The following example starts a run with a custom message describing the changes.

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start ws-abc123 --message "Deploying version 2.0"
```

### Start a run with debugging enabled

The following example starts a run with debugging mode enabled for troubleshooting.

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start ws-abc123 --debugging-mode
```
